finding: The first manually read dial-bezel layout bounds conflicted with direct circle detection and would have triggered an unjustified scale change.

rejected_change.proposed_action: increase radial cage scale from manual component-layout severity
rejected_change.reason: A constrained Hough-circle observation found a source circle diameter of approximately 266.6 px / 386 px = 0.691, while the controlled candidate bezel mask width is 0.701. The difference is within the interpretation uncertainty of the perspective product image.

retained_observations: The candidate DialFace normalized width is 0.629; a source inner-circle candidate from the same constrained observation is approximately 242.4 px / 386 px = 0.628.

The top control is visibly narrower and substantially shorter above the housing than the source reading; its source boundary is higher confidence because its silver silhouette is distinct from the black/red body.
next_action: Scale the independently manufactured TopControl cage, then re-render the controlled component mask and compare only the supported top-control change.
claim_boundary: Circle detection is an observed image cue, not calibrated geometry or proof of a final reference match. The rejected dial edit demonstrates that component-layout evidence must be reconciled before mutation.
